**Verdict: don't publish as written. One claim has to go.**

**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Plastic-Free Tea Bags" | Allowlisted (supplier certificate, EN 13432) |
| "Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable." | Allowlisted, exact wording |
| "Recommended by nutritionists." | **Unsupported** |

**Problem**
- "Recommended by nutritionists." is an invented endorsement. Nothing in the policy or this conversation shows any nutritionist recommends Pebblebrook. It also implies a health benefit, and the policy rules out health claims of any kind. Search ad platforms are likely to flag it too. If it's true, we'd need a named source and the policy updated, and the landing page would have to make the same claim.

**Compliant version**

- Headline: Plastic-Free Tea Bags (21 characters)
- Description: Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable. (51 characters)

If you'd like to use the remaining space, these are all on the allowlist: "Free UK delivery on orders over £25." or "Every tin is packed by hand in Bristol." Make sure the landing page also carries any claim the ad uses. Sam needs to approve it before it goes live.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "Recommended by nutritionists.", "type": "fake_testimonial"}], "publish": false}
```
